messages:
maya-ml: running the continuous-batcher sims with spikey traffic (Poisson baseline + Pareto microbursts) across APAC (h100) and EU (g8). want to surface long-tail sensitivity and kernel choice cost tradeoffs. attached perf dumps soon.

sam-runtime: nice. what's the load shape? steady qps then random spikes?

maya-ml: yep. baseline 50 qps, spikes to 1000 qps for 1-3s every ~90s, plus a small embedding-heavy cohort (short prompts, small outputs).

leo-eng: curious if max_batch_tokens or window size helps more for those 1-3s bursts. we saw weird fairness inversion last week.

carmen-sre: also need to know cold-KV cache impact on tail — spikes that hit cold models blow p99.

maya-ml: ran 3 configs:
```
A) window=15ms, max_batch_tokens=1024, kernel=fast-attn-v1
B) window=40ms, max_batch_tokens=4096, kernel=tiling-quant
C) dynamic-window (15->60ms), max_batch_tokens=2048, kernel=hybrid-tilt
```
results summary below. cpu/gpu util and eviction logs attached.

benchmark-bot: summary: median latency (inference-only, tokens/sec normalized):
- APAC/h100 A: 11.8ms median, p95 86ms, p99 320ms, throughput avg 820 t/s during bursts
- EU/g8 B: 18.5ms median, p95 140ms, p99 560ms, throughput avg 420 t/s during bursts

sam-runtime: so h100 handles bursts much better as expected. how about fairness across tenants? any starvation?

maya-ml: config A (short window) had lowest median but p99 spikes worse — fast-attn-v1 has low setup overhead so good for small batches, but microburst packing fails for heterogeneous workloads: the embedding cohort kept stealing slots -> high tail for text customers.

leo-eng: config B (larger window) smoothed tail on g8 but increased median. also saw increased KV eviction rate by ~2.6x in APAC, probably cache churn from bigger batches.

carmen-sre: can you paste the eviction snippet?

maya-ml: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 14:22:03] evict key model:v1:kv shard=3 reason=coalesce_resize latency_ms=2
[2026-03-18 14:22:03] load key model:v1:kv shard=3 warmup_tokens=128
[2026-03-18 14:22:05] evict key model:v1:kv shard=3 reason=burst_overflow
```

sam-runtime: interesting. dynamic-window C? did it trade off well?

maya-ml: dynamic-window was best overall: median slightly higher than A (14ms) but p99 180ms vs 320ms for A on h100. throughput during bursts close to A. it reduced tenant starvation by enabling short-term higher batching for heavy cohorts and short windows for latency-sensitive ones.

leo-eng: kernel choices — tiling-quant cut GPU mem and improved throughput on g8 but increased per-request unpack cost; hybrid-tilt on h100 gave best overall stable tail under mixed load.

carmen-sre: any numbers on cost per 1M tokens for each config? we need to present to pricing.

maya-ml: rough cost estimates (infra-only):
- A/h100: $22 per 1M tokens (lower median but high tail -> potential SLO penalties)
- B/g8: $14 per 1M tokens (higher median, smoother tails for g8-like infra)
- C/h100 hybrid: $19 per 1M tokens (best SLO hit rate, moderate cost)

sam-runtime: good. what's our recommendation for Dedicated pools vs Hosted API for bursty customers?

maya-ml: for bursty workloads with mixed cohorts, recommend Dedicated with dynamic-window policy + hybrid-tilt kernel on h100. Hosted API can use dynamic-window but fallback kernel mapping to quant-tiling for cost when load is stable.

leo-eng: can we automate warmup tokens on model switch to reduce p99? looks like 128 warmup tokens helped but cost is small compared to p99 savings.

maya-ml: agree. adding a lightweight warmup stage on model swap reduced p99 by ~35% in sims. will add a PR for autosuggested warmup=64/128 based on model size.

benchmark-bot: attachments: perf_plots: https://perf.internal/redwood/2251236789/plots (latency histograms, throughput timelines), raw-csv: https://perf.internal/redwood/2251236789/csv.

carmen-sre: filing postmortem template for potential SLO changes if we flip defaults. @sam-runtime pls review kernel fallback policy.

sam-runtime: on it. quick follow-up: can we run a longer 24h sim with the same spike pattern but randomized seed to validate stability?

maya-ml: yep scheduling now, will post results tomorrow. thanks all :rocket:
